payload.title: The ledger migration ignores a constraint that already exists under the same name even when its definition differs, and `finding-event-ledger mirror` refuses forever once an old-vocabulary row exists without naming a remedy
evidence: tools/gates/finding-event-ledger.ts:173-183 (mirror refuses rows that are not git lines and names the rows, not what to do)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a mismatch is not hidden behind an ignored error, and a refusal names its remedy
payload.notes: A finding_events_git_mirror_chk that exists with another definition makes up() a silent no-op, so the new rows are bound by the old check. The ledger table is immutable by trigger, so one old-vocabulary row makes every later mirror run refuse; the refusal lists the rows but names neither the parity command nor the operator step. Read from the code, not probed; the ledger is not wired to a lane yet, so no row of the old vocabulary is known to exist. Close condition: up() reads the existing constraint's definition (pg_get_constraintdef) and fails when it differs from the intended one, instead of swallowing duplicate_object. The mirror refusal names `finding-event-ledger parity` and the operator step for rows the registry does not hold. A test for each.
